product_overview: Stabilize the BS-OPT developer stack by fixing the ruff configuration, removing startup script redundancy, enabling containerized debugging, and adding observability/middleware so developers can reliably start, lint, debug, and validate the API.
core_goals: Fix pyproject.toml Ruff configuration so `ruff check .` runs without parse errors
Refactor scripts/start_all_dev.sh to delegate infra startup and remove redundant Docker logic
Enable standard remote debug ports (Python 5678, Node 9229) in dev Dockerfiles
Introduce structured request/response logging middleware and expose Prometheus metrics for verification
Provide fast developer verification flows (health, metrics, auth, pricing) to validate environment correctness

features.name: Lint Configuration Fix
features.description: Fix the [tool.ruff.lint] section in pyproject.toml to use correct map/dictionary syntax for per-file-ignores so `ruff check .` does not crash.
user_flows: GET / -> Receive 200 with message 'BS-Opt Optimized API' -> GET /health -> Receive 200 {"status":"healthy"} -> GET /metrics -> Receive 200 Prometheus metrics text
GET /api/v1/auth/me without Authorization header -> Receive 401 Unauthorized

features.name: Startup Script: start_all_dev.sh Delegation
features.description: Refactor scripts/start_all_dev.sh to detect existing infra and delegate to scripts/start_infra.sh if necessary, eliminating duplicated docker-compose logic and 'slop' execution.
user_flows: GET /metrics -> Receive 200 Prometheus metrics text -> POST /api/v1/auth/login with valid credentials {"email":"dev@example.com","password":"password"} -> Receive 200 with access_token and token_type bearer -> GET /api/v1/auth/me with Authorization: Bearer <access_token> -> Receive 200 user profile
POST /api/v1/auth/login with valid credentials while auth-service is unreachable -> Receive 503 Service Unavailable (connection/refused) or network timeout

features.name: Developer Debugging Ports
features.description: Expose and document standard debug ports in dev Dockerfiles so developers can attach debuggers (Python debugpy 5678, Node --inspect 9229) while the stack runs in containers.
user_flows: POST /api/v1/auth/login with valid credentials {"email":"dev@example.com","password":"password"} -> Receive 200 with access_token -> POST /graphql with Authorization: Bearer <access_token> and a valid introspection query -> Receive 200 GraphQL response
POST /graphql with malformed query body -> Receive 400 or 200 with GraphQL errors indicating malformed request

features.name: Request/Response Logging Middleware
features.description: Add structured logging middleware that emits request payload, response status, and duration for each HTTP API call; expose timing metrics to Prometheus.
user_flows: POST /api/v1/pricing/calculate with valid body {"s":100,"k":100,"t":0.5,"r":0.01,"sigma":0.2,"option_type":"call","model":"black_scholes"} with Authorization: Bearer <access_token> -> Receive 200 {"price": number, "greeks": {...}} -> GET /metrics -> Receive 200 Prometheus metrics text containing a histogram/counter for /api/v1/pricing/calculate request duration
POST /api/v1/pricing/calculate with missing required field 's' -> Receive 422 Validation error

features.name: Authentication
features.description: Register, login, refresh tokens, logout, and get current user profile with RS256 JWT tokens and refresh support. This is used both by app flows and by startup verification.
user_flows: POST /api/v1/auth/register with body {"email":"newuser@example.com","password":"P@ssw0rd","full_name":"New User"} -> Receive 201 User object with JWT token -> POST /api/v1/auth/login with body {"email":"newuser@example.com","password":"P@ssw0rd"} -> Receive 200 {"access_token":"...","token_type":"bearer"} -> GET /api/v1/auth/me with Authorization: Bearer <access_token> -> Receive 200 User profile
POST /api/v1/auth/register with body containing an email already registered -> Receive 409 Email already registered -> POST /api/v1/auth/login with wrong password -> Receive 401 Invalid credentials

features.name: Pricing Calculation
features.description: Calculate option prices using Black-Scholes, Heston FFT, or LSM models via a secured endpoint used for verification of numerics and middleware.
user_flows: POST /api/v1/pricing/calculate with Authorization: Bearer <access_token> and body {"s":100,"k":110,"t":0.25,"r":0.02,"sigma":0.25,"option_type":"put","model":"black_scholes"} -> Receive 200 {"price": number, "greeks": {...}}
POST /api/v1/pricing/calculate with Authorization: Bearer <access_token> and body specifying invalid model {"model":"unknown_model", ...} -> Receive 422 Validation error

features.name: Portfolio Management
features.description: CRUD operations on user portfolios; used by developers to verify that DB migrations and startup have completed correctly.
user_flows: POST /api/v1/portfolio/positions with Authorization: Bearer <access_token> and body {"symbol":"AAPL","quantity":10,"entry_price":150} -> Receive 201 Created position -> GET /api/v1/portfolio with Authorization: Bearer <access_token> -> Receive 200 Portfolio object including new position -> DELETE /api/v1/portfolio/positions/{id} with Authorization: Bearer <access_token> for returned id -> Receive 200 Success
DELETE /api/v1/portfolio/positions/{id} with Authorization: Bearer <access_token} for non-existent id -> Receive 404 Position not found

features.name: Health & Observability
features.description: Lightweight endpoints to verify service liveness and Prometheus metrics for observability; these are primary verification points in startup flows.
user_flows: GET /health -> Receive 200 {"status":"healthy"} -> GET /metrics -> Receive 200 Prometheus metrics text
GET /api/v1/users/me without Authorization header -> Receive 401 Unauthorized

features.name: GraphQL API Verification
features.description: GraphQL endpoint provides flexible querying for integration tests and developer inspection; include it in verification flows to ensure schema is available after startup.
user_flows: POST /graphql with a valid query or introspection query -> Receive 200 GraphQL response with data -> POST /api/v1/auth/refresh with a valid refresh_token -> Receive 200 New access token (when required by mutation flows)
POST /graphql with invalid/malicious query -> Receive 400 or a 200 GraphQL response containing errors
